records.title: GexMolGen: cross-modal generation of hit-like molecules via large language model encoding of gene expression signatures

scope.decision_rationale: This is a new generative model for molecules from gene expression signatures, so the biological modality is central. The only language-model mention is scGPT used as a single-cell genetic encoder; no natural-language text component or text-bio mapping is described.
scope.evidence_snippet: “advanced single-cell large language model called scGPT as the genetic encoder” and “encode pre- and post-perturbation gene expressions”

architecture.decision_rationale: The paper proposes a new cross-modal generator, not a wrapper, and explicitly says it "generates hit-like molecules" and "decoded into molecular graphs." It also cites foundation-model-style pretraining via scGPT and a pre-trained scaffold-based molecular model.

records.title: Rethinking Genomic Modeling Through Optical Character Recognition

scope.decision_rationale: Primary model paper introducing OpticalDNA. It models DNA as OCR-style document understanding with a visual DNA encoder and document decoder, so the biological modality, text/document component, and bridge are all central.
scope.evidence_snippet: “reframes genomic modeling as Optical Character Recognition (OCR)-style document understanding”; “trains an OCR-capable vision-language model with a visual DNA encoder and a document decoder”

architecture.decision_rationale: The paper presents OpticalDNA as a new model with a visual encoder and document decoder, trained on prompt-conditioned tasks over genomic primitives. It also frames the work as genomic foundation modeling with broad benchmark evaluation and strong transfer across long-context tasks.
